clue.text: Fairly reasonable collection is taken in church

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the church abbreviation is split around the other pieces

parts.note: a heap is a collection or pile of things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A modest collection is gathered during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fairly reasonable in price is moderately inexpensive, the -ish suffix softening the adjective.

clue.text: Figure quoted in Hackney, £ 0.00?

indicators.note: quoted in Hackney means spoken in a Cockney accent, where the th sound becomes f

parts.note: the figure here is the number three

explanation.surface: A price tag in an East London borough shows nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a district of East London; in a Cockney accent 'three' is said as 'free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costing nothing, zero pounds and zero pence, is offered without charge.

clue.text: See 24
A couple of ways to rise from a gland

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means each road word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, one kind of way
a lane is a second kind of way

explanation.surface: Something is secreted upward from a gland via two routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns each way in place: RD becomes DR and LANE becomes ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal is a gland sitting atop each kidney, the word serving as a noun for the organ.

clue.text: Animal having to munch through fruit

indicators.note: through means one piece is set inside the other, passing into its middle

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to munch is to eat

explanation.surface: Some creature has to chew its way through a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape, such as a gorilla or chimpanzee, is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Rep was beaten up with scoundrel, one getting booted

indicators.note: beaten up means knocked about, so the letters of the first words are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder
a heel is a contemptible scoundrel

explanation.surface: A sales rep was assaulted alongside some villain, one of them kicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' rearranges REP and WAS into SPAREW. 'booted' suggests kicking; the spare tyre is kept in a car's boot (British for trunk).
explanation.definitionFit: A spare wheel is stored in the boot of a car, so it is what gets put in the boot.

clue.text: See 8
Hood fortress, we gathered?

indicators.note: gathered means collected together in a jumble, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: We infer this place was Robin Hood's stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all of HOOD, FORTRESS and WE, and the whole clue defines the woodland where Robin Hood's outlaws hid.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes this Nottinghamshire woodland the refuge and stronghold of the outlaw Robin Hood.

clue.text: Eagle, perhaps, has to crack rock

parts.note: a crack can be a sharp blow or knock, a rap
a tor is a rocky outcrop or hill

explanation.surface: An eagle must split open stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is one example of a raptor, a bird of prey.

clue.text: See 24
See 14
Frame, almost nothing to carry round a very short distance

indicators.note: to carry round means the shortened word holds the other pieces inside it
almost means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: zero means nothing
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
MM is the abbreviation for millimetre, a very short distance

explanation.surface: Something framed holds almost nothing over a tiny span.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like a verb but is the definition; 'almost' trims the last letter of the word for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zimmer is the trade name of a walking frame used by the elderly or infirm.

clue.text: Singing, one taking transport uphill to see capoeira, say

indicators.note: in a down clue going uphill means reading the whole run from bottom to top

parts.note: tra-la is a cheery bit of singing
one is the Roman numeral I
a tram is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A singer takes a tram up the hill to watch a Brazilian dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' turns the whole run TRALAITRAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Capoeira is a Brazilian fighting discipline mixing dance and combat, an example of the category.

clue.text: On holiday in an enchanted garden, say, easily distracted

parts.note: someone on holiday is away
in an enchanted garden you would be in the company of fairies

explanation.surface: Someone on vacation in a magical garden loses concentration easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone dreamy and not paying attention to what is going on.

clue.text: Occasion for early kicking creating hysteria with child

indicators.note: creating suggests making something new out of the following letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something causes a fuss with a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The Charity Shield was the English football match opening the season in August, so the kicking comes early.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charity Shield was the curtain-raising football match played at the start of each English season.

clue.text: Kinky full S & M

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the spelt-out letters are rearranged

parts.note: S in full is the compass point south
the ampersand stands for the word and

explanation.surface: Kinky sadomasochism is the whole hog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S & M' suggests sadomasochism, but S is read in full as SOUTH and 'Kinky' rearranges it to THOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: M is the Roman numeral for one thousand.

clue.text: Number like itself written in pen

indicators.note: written in means set inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
even means equal, level, like itself

explanation.surface: A figure is copied out in ink, just as it appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy is a number, seven tens.

clue.text: Fool, singer and birdwatcher

parts.note: a twit is a fool
Cher is a famous American singer

explanation.surface: A list of people: an idiot, a vocalist and a bird enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is British slang for an obsessive birdwatcher who travels to see rare species.

clue.text: Two Conservative leaders overseeing a holiday destination

indicators.note: in a down clue overseeing means placed above what follows

parts.note: John Major was a Conservative leader and prime minister
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A pair of Tory leaders supervise a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca, a Spanish Balearic island, is a popular holiday spot.

clue.text: Canadian province with idiot president, degree going to head

indicators.note: going to head means the degree letters shift to the front of the whole

parts.note: a nit is an idiot
Obama was a US president
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A Canadian region has a foolish leader, whose qualification goes to his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to head' moves MA from the end of NITOBAMA to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the prairie provinces of Canada.

clue.text: A celebrity unknown, not written down, becoming killer

indicators.note: in a down clue not written down means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a name is a celebrity, as in a big name
X is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An anonymous star, unrecorded, turns murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not written down' means written upwards in this down light, turning NAMEX into XEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An axeman is a murderer who uses an axe.

clue.text: Revolutionary colours invisible for the bloody right-wing politician

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, so the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Insurgent flags hidden for a hated hard-right leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian media tycoon and prime minister led a right-wing party; 'bloody' is the setter's jibe.

clue.text: See 15
See 22
Juvenile competition hurrying along unemployment figures?

parts.note: the sack is dismissal from a job, leading to unemployment
to race is to hurry along

explanation.surface: Children's contest that speeds along the jobless numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a children's sports-day event where competitors hop in sacks.

clue.text: Rubbish swimmer rushes up to see PR man

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is rubbish
a cod is a fish, a swimmer
nips means dashes or rushes

explanation.surface: A useless fish dashes upstream to meet a publicist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a public relations adviser who puts a favourable slant on news.

clue.text: Unable to conceive aristo getting heard

indicators.note: getting heard means the word is said aloud and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: a baron is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A nobleman who cannot father children gets a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren describes someone or something infertile, unable to produce offspring.

clue.text: Herb, reversing into US school, crashed

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school in American usage

indicators.note: reversing means the herb's name is read backwards

parts.note: dill is a herb

explanation.surface: Someone named Herb backed his car into an American school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' poses as a man's name in the surface but is just the plant; 'reversing' turns it round before it goes into the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Collided means crashed together.
